quote: I think the average that I've seen is between 1,100 and 1,400 around that range per month because I do have an EV as well.
stewart_read: An EV adds substantial electric load, which is a strong solar-fit signal and a qualification-boosting detail. The rep acknowledges it warmly but never reflects it back as a reason solar makes even more sense for her specifically.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to tie high-usage disclosures (EV, kWh range) directly back to the value of solar for that household rather than just filing the detail and moving to small talk — this schema principle isn't yet Ion-populated for demographics, but the missed anchor-and-flip move itself is visible and coachable regardless.

quote: is solar kind of usable in Illinois because some of the colder months are pretty brutal.
stewart_read: This is a live, substantive product-fit concern — the customer is directly asking whether solar works in her climate — and it is never answered anywhere in the call, not even with a redirect to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be deliberately reserving this for the specialist's technical walkthrough rather than answering it himself.
coaching_implication: Even if deferring to the specialist is the right call, the rep should have explicitly bridged it ('great question, my specialist will walk through your specific production numbers for Illinois winters') so the customer isn't left wondering if it was heard. As it stands, this concern is unresolved and should be flagged directly to the closer.

quote: I got I got a quote from Sunrun roughly around $1.60 something a month. And so I thought that wasn't bad with the with the battery with two batteries.
stewart_read: The customer names a specific competitor, a specific monthly price, and a specific battery configuration unprompted. This is a gift of competitive intelligence that the rep should probe and log for the closer, but instead the rep pivots straight into Ion's own battery lineup without confirming or repeating back the Sunrun numbers.
coaching_implication: This should be logged verbatim in the closer's brief rather than left buried in the transcript — coach the rep to repeat competitive numbers back ('so Sunrun quoted you around $160/month with two Powerwalls — good to know') to both confirm accuracy and signal attentiveness.

quote: But so I kinda look at that way. I was like, yeah. It may not be the best car, but like, overall, looks wise, but it is the most reliable when it comes to going somewhere.
stewart_read: The rep opens a multi-turn personal conversation about EV brands and charging networks that has no bearing on solar qualification. It's rapport-building but drifts well past the verify section's purpose and adds no qualification value.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a deliberate rapport-building move given the calm, comparison-shopping customer, and it doesn't appear to cost the appointment.
coaching_implication: Flag as a time-management habit to watch — rapport tangents are fine in small doses but this one runs several exchanges (04:20-05:26) without redirecting back to qualification content.

quote: I I'm not exactly sure just because I'm I'm just a scheduler, so I don't really know the specific details. But I do think that we have a fifteen year plan, and I think we have I think we offer a couple different ones.
stewart_read: Rep admits the limits of his role transparently rather than fabricating plan terms — a disciplined recovery from a knowledge gap, even though the underlying question (plan length) still goes unanswered.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the right pattern (admit + redirect) but pair it with an explicit note-taking confirmation so the customer knows the question is captured, not dropped.

quote: Yeah. And I would say I don't know if you were doing, like, any, like, quote generators online or anything. But those ones, if you have done those, those won't be as accurate
stewart_read: The customer just voiced a cost-skepticism objection ('something's not adding up') that is a textbook objection_inversion trigger. The rep addresses it informationally (accuracy of quote generators) rather than flipping it into alignment against the current high-bill status quo.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's informational response is reasonable damage control since the customer's confusion is about competing numbers, not about affordability itself, so a flip may not fit cleanly here.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on redirecting cost-confusion moments toward what the bill/utility currently costs her, reinforcing urgency rather than just explaining quote-generator inaccuracy.

quote: I will get you on our schedule for Friday the eighth at 3PM, you said. Right?
stewart_read: The booking itself is clean and specific (day + time), but the call ends without a recap of the unresolved plan-length question or the climate-viability concern, leaving those as loose threads for the closer to walk into cold.
coaching_implication: Coach button-up discipline: before closing, the rep should recap open questions ('I'll make sure the specialist covers the plan length and how solar performs in our winters') so the customer feels heard and the closer has a clear brief.
